title: When the Rivergate Sings
premise: Mara Lockridge, a desert ranger who has spent a decade erasing herself from every record, is pulled back into the world when an upriver salvage expedition goes silent. The thief she was tracking turns out to be her estranged half-brother, carrying proof that the Lockridge fortune—and the river town of Rivergate itself—was built on a drowned massacre the family has spent generations burying. Racing the corrupt salvage fleet and the coming monsoon, Mara must choose between reclaiming her inheritance or burning it. She reaches the wreck by the sixth tide, floods the evidence loose to the whole valley, and walks away from the name Lockridge with a found family of her own choosing.
about_author: Noor Eastwick is the pen name of a former river guide turned novelist who writes adventure stories about people who'd rather not be heroes. They live somewhere between two watersheds and write at dawn, when the fog still owns the water.

chapters.title: Nothing Out Here Answers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Tracking a thief across the salt flats, she reads sign like scripture and catches only a ghost: a dropped radio handset stamped with an expedition call sign from upriver. When she raises the frequency, static answers—then cuts off mid-word. Emotional beat: the loneliness she chose suddenly feels like exile.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Mara plays the corrupted final transmission for the ranger station's aging dispatcher, Odile, who recognizes the voice as her nephew's. Command refuses to authorize a search until after monsoon season. Emotional beat: quiet fury; Mara realizes bureaucracy will let people drown on schedule.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Odile's charts show the monsoon makes landfall in six tidal cycles; after that, the river gorge becomes unnavigable. Mara resigns her post, takes a skiff, and heads upriver alone. Emotional beat: cold resolve masking fear as she leaves the desert that defined her.

chapters.title: The Fleet at Anchor
chapters.summary: At the river mouth, Mara sees the Voss salvage fleet loading armed crews—the same company whose barge the missing expedition was surveying for. She slips past their picket at night. POV shifts briefly to fleet captain Ilsa Voss, who knows exactly what the expedition found. Emotional beat: dread; the enemy is organized and patient.

chapters.title: A Thief in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Mara ambushes the thief from her original trail—only to find Tam Lockridge, the half-brother erased from her life twenty years ago. He stole from Voss, not the expedition. He claims he can prove what's under the river. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Drowned
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Around a driftwood fire, he tells her: the 1911 Lockridge barge didn't sink—it was scuttled with striking dockworkers aboard, and the expedition found the hull intact, with the manifest inside. Emotional beat: Mara's inherited pride cracking against inherited guilt.

chapters.title: The Silent Camp
chapters.summary: They reach the expedition's camp: tents slashed, gear looted, no bodies. A survivor's chalk arrow points upriver toward the gorge. Mara realizes Voss got here first but missed someone. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into urgency.

chapters.title: Rapids and Rust
chapters.summary: Running the first gorge rapids, they wreck the skiff and lose most of their supplies. Sheltering in a rusted lockhouse, they find expedition survivor Priya Chandrasekar, injured and hiding, who confirms Voss's divers reached the wreck. Emotional beat: fragile relief—three is a crew now.

chapters.title: Ilsa Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV chapter. She interrogates her captured expedition leader, revealing she's not just salvaging—she's destroying the manifest for the families who profited, including the Lockridges. Emotional beat: chilling competence; Voss believes she's keeping the peace.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Priya reveals the expedition leader sold them out to Voss for his family's safety. Mara confronts the idea that everyone serves power somehow—including her grandfather, whose ledgers Tam carries. Emotional beat: disillusionment deepening into purpose.

chapters.title: Tide Three
chapters.summary: With three tides left, they portage around the second gorge using a cable tram Tam repairs from childhood memory—he grew up on this river too. First real trust between siblings. Emotional beat: tentative warmth, the first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Narrows
chapters.summary: Voss's gunboat corners them in the narrows. Priya creates a diversion with flares while Mara runs the boat through a flooded side channel no chart shows. They escape but Priya is wounded. Emotional beat: terror and guilt; Mara's invisibility skills now cost others.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Cutter Bend
chapters.summary: They shelter with Wren, a river hermit who tends graves of the 1911 dead—descendants of survivors who never spoke. Wren gives them a storm-proof route and blesses the journey. Emotional beat: Mara sees what inheritance could mean if reclaimed rather than renounced.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam secretly radios Voss, offering the ledgers in exchange for letting Mara go. Mara overhears. Confrontation: he did it because he thinks she'll die otherwise, repeating their father's pattern of deciding for family. Emotional beat: rage, then understanding—they're both protecting each other badly.

chapters.title: Tide Five
chapters.summary: One tide left. They run the last gorge at night through rising wind, Priya navigating by the old lock lights Wren showed them. Voss's fleet shadows them, waiting for the storm to do its work. Emotional beat: exhausted determination; the river forgives nothing.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Meridian
chapters.summary: They reach the sunken barge in the flooded quarry pool. Diving the cold water, Mara finds the hold: bones, and the manifest sealed in a copper case—her family's signature on the scuttling order. Emotional beat: horror and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Voss's boarding party takes the site, holding them at gunpoint as the monsoon's first squall hits. Voss offers Mara the same bargain her grandfather made: silence, wealth, belonging. Emotional beat: temptation offered honestly—and refused.

chapters.title: When the Rivergate Sings
chapters.summary: Climax. As the storm peaks, Mara opens the quarry's floodgates, letting the river surge through and carry the manifest, the bones' testimony, and Voss's divers' equipment downstream into public view. In the chaos, Priya and Tam seize the gunboat. Emotional beat: cathartic release—the river finally speaks.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Storm's aftermath. Voss, stranded and exposed, negotiates rather than drowns; her backers' names surface with the wreckage. The expedition survivors are found alive in a sea cave. Emotional beat: exhausted reckoning; truth costs less than silence, in the end.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Mara stands before the valley assembly as the manifest is read aloud. Offered the Lockridge seat and name, she transfers the estate into a trust for the 1911 descendants and the river towns. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into repair.

chapters.title: Crew of the Skiff
chapters.summary: Quiet denouement. Mara, Tam, Priya, and Wren rebuild the skiff together. Tam asks where she'll go; Mara says downriver, then wherever the crew decides. Emotional beat: warmth without sentimentality—family chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The River Forgets Less
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Mara's POV. Months later, patrolling again but no longer invisible, she passes Rivergate where new markers name the drowned. The river sings under the bridge, and this time she stops to listen. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
